hero.subtitle: When a death in Santa Rosa was caused by someone else's carelessness, your family has a civil path forward under California law. We can help you explore your options at no cost, so you can focus on grieving.

about.title: Santa Rosa Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Rosa recorded 8 traffic deaths in 2025, alongside 562 injury collisions across the city. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Sonoma County trying to figure out what comes next. Some of those losses happened on US-101 as it threads through town; others on Stony Point Road, Santa Rosa Avenue, or Route 12, corridors that carry the heaviest collision counts in the public record. Fatal harm is not limited to the road, either. A fall at a business, an error in medical care, or an unsafe worksite can leave a family in the same place. California allows a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children to bring a wrongful death action, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in some situations. The claim can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. It runs on its own track, entirely separate from any criminal case. We handle wrongful death claims on contingency—your family pays nothing out of pocket unless we recover on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Rosa Families Choose Us

items.title: Standing Questions Answered Early
items.desc: California limits who may file, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out quickly whether you and other relatives qualify.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Watched Closely
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity such as the city or Caltrans is involved. Getting started early protects that deadline.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Our service is free, and we work on contingency. Your family pays nothing out of pocket to pursue funeral costs, lost support, and the loss of companionship.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash on Santa Rosa Avenue is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, the two are separate. A criminal case is brought by the Sonoma County District Attorney and focuses on punishment, not on what your family lost. A wrongful death claim is a civil action you control, and it can proceed whether or not charges are filed or result in a conviction. We can explain how the two may affect each other.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there is no one in that group, certain dependents or heirs may have standing. Because these rules can get complicated in blended families, it helps to have an attorney review your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Santa Rosa?
items.answer: Generally, two years from the date of death. If a public agency may share responsibility, for example a claim involving a city street or a state highway like US-101, the deadline to give notice is much shorter. Reaching out sooner rather than later keeps every option open.
